results.question: Do creatures phasing back in trigger enter the battlefield abilities?
results.text:
No — creatures that phase in do not trigger enter-the-battlefield abilities.

Phasing is a static ability that changes how permanents behave during the untap step: phased-in permanents with phasing phase out and phased-out permanents that phased out under that player’s control phase in (702.26a), and when a permanent phases in its status becomes “phased in” and the game again treats it as though it exists (702.26c). Enters-the-battlefield abilities are zone-change triggers that trigger when a permanent actually enters the battlefield (603.6a). Phasing isn’t a zone change (a phased-out permanent isn’t treated as having left the battlefield), and rule 702.26d explicitly states that “Zone-change triggers don’t trigger when a permanent phases in or out.” Therefore a creature phasing in does not cause enters-the-battlefield triggers to trigger. The only special “look back in time” exception shown in the provided rules applies to abilities that trigger when a permanent phases out (603.10b) and does not make phasing in count as entering the battlefield. Also note that abilities that trigger when a permanent becomes attached or unattached don’t trigger when that permanent phases in or out (702.26j).

Assumption: No additional card-specific text in this situation changes the general rules given above; the provided rules are sufficient to answer the question.
